html:
The Emberá Katío, also called Eyabida ("mountain people"), are the highland branch of the Emberá, an Indigenous people of north-west Colombia. They live in the forested hills and river valleys of Antioquia, Córdoba and Chocó, around the upper Sinú and San Jorge rivers. Their language belongs to the Chocoan family, shared with other Emberá groups such as the Eperara and with the Wounaan.

They live in scattered households, farming maize, plantains and cassava, and hunting and fishing. The Urrá dam on the Sinú, built in the 1990s, flooded part of their land, and leaders who opposed it were killed during Colombia's armed conflict. Many families have been driven to cities such as Bogotá and Medellín.
